historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (pre-spin consolidated entity; used only as a loose cross-check -- see notes)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs above (FY2020-FY2025) describe the PRE-SPIN CONSOLIDATED entity, which included the divested Biosciences & Diagnostics business, and are NOT the basis for the forward growth path in assumptions.base -- that path is instead built bottom-up from the FY2026 quarterly print cadence and management's FY2026 guidance (see inputs.notes). Reported equity CAGR is depressed/negative largely by buybacks, debt-funded acquisitions and pension items over the period rather than a shrinking business; EPS CAGR is distorted by the Q1 FY2026 separation-related net loss (-$311M net income that quarter) and does not reflect New BD's underlying run-rate (adjusted EPS guidance is $12.62-12.72 for FY2026, growth of 6.1-6.9%).

scenario_narratives.base: New BD executes its standalone MedTech strategy broadly as guided -- mid-single-digit organic growth led by BioPharma Systems' GLP-1 tailwind and Interventional, with the BD Excellence program and improved segment mix lifting adjusted EBITDA margin from the mid-20s toward the high-20s over the decade, while leverage glides toward the ~2.5x long-term target.
scenario_narratives.bull: GLP-1/biologics demand and Neopak capacity expansion outrun BD's own targets, Alaris/quality-remediation overhang resolves faster than expected, and tuck-in M&A funded by the deleveraged post-spin balance sheet adds incremental growth without diluting margin -- New BD re-rates as a focused, faster-growing pure-play medtech.
scenario_narratives.bear: Alaris/consent-decree remediation and post-spin separation dis-synergies persist longer than guided, hospital capex cyclicality pressures equipment sales, GLP-1 drug-delivery share gains undershoot the ~$1B-by-2030 target against competing capacity, and input-cost/tariff inflation outpaces BD Excellence productivity gains.

valuation_philosophy.summary: New BD is valued as a standalone pure-play medtech company on an owner-FCF basis, using a FY2026 revenue base built from post-spin run-rate evidence (management's disclosed pro-forma FY2024 New BD revenue grown at guided/actual organic rates, cross-checked against the FY2026 quarterly cadence) rather than the pre-spin consolidated entity's historical trend, which would overstate both the size and the margin mix of the retained business. The valuation credits management's stated (and already partly executed) capital-allocation plan -- debt paydown toward a ~2.5x net-leverage target and buybacks funded by the $4B Waters transaction proceeds -- through the Q2 FY2026 balance sheet, and assumes further margin expansion from the BD Excellence productivity program and the removal of the lower-margin Biosciences & Diagnostics mix, tempered by a live, well-documented regulatory/quality overhang (Alaris/CareFusion) that is charged into a higher-than-default bear-case weight rather than into the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Base-year revenue and margin are house estimates bridging two data sources (pro-forma FY2024 disclosure, actual FY2026 quarterly prints) because the DB/Metrics CSV has not yet been updated for a clean, fully-parsed 'New BD' standalone revenue and margin series -- a subsequent 10-K/10-Q parse with an explicit pro-forma comparative could move the base by a low-single-digit percentage.

Net debt and share count are anchored to the Q2 FY2026 (31-Mar-2026) balance sheet, not the more recent Q3 FY2026 (30-Jun-2026) figures referenced in the Analysis JSON's recent_developments (not yet in the parsed DB) -- further buyback/debt-paydown activity through Q3-Q4 FY2026 likely makes both net debt and share count somewhat lower than modeled here, making this valuation mildly conservative on that dimension.

Alaris/CareFusion FDA consent-decree remediation and broader quality-system warning letters (Dispensing, Specimen Management) are an open-ended cost and distraction risk; a further enforcement action or penalty is not modeled as its own scenario but sits inside the bear case's higher probability weight.

D&A percentage is carried over from the pre-spin consolidated FY2025 ratio on the assumption that acquisition-intangible amortization sits mostly in the retained MedTech businesses; if a materially different share of Bard/CareFusion intangible amortization went with the divested Biosciences & Diagnostics unit, the true New BD D&A (and therefore near-term FCF) could differ from this estimate.

GLP-1/biologics drug-delivery demand is a structural growth driver in the base and bull cases but is competitive (other prefillable-syringe/glass suppliers are also expanding capacity) and its ~$1B-by-2030 contribution is a management target, not a guaranteed outcome.

inputs.sbc_source: H1 FY2026 cash-flow SBC add-back $149M annualized (x2) against H1 FY2026 revenue $9,200M = 3.2% of revenue; FY2025 consolidated SBC was only 1.2% of revenue because the divested, lower-SBC-intensity Biosciences & Diagnostics business diluted the ratio -- post-spin New BD carries a similar SBC dollar pool on a smaller revenue base, so the ratio rose materially.
inputs.wacc_rationale: US large-cap medtech, investment-grade credit but elevated leverage (~2.6x net debt/EBITDA at deal close, targeting ~2.5x long-term). Risk-free ~4.2% (10Y UST), ERP ~5%, levered beta ~0.8-0.9 for defensive medtech with above-average leverage post-Waters-transaction debt paydown in progress. WACC set at 7.5%.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial to this filer's cash flow statement relative to revenue; not separately modeled (no dedicated lease_cost_pct_path).
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interests disclosed; net income is fully attributable to BD shareholders.
inputs.notes: Fresh build. Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md as a standard US operating-company owner-FCF DCF -- BD is a diversified medtech manufacturer/distributor with no bank/REIT/LIC/holdco/distressed characteristics. On 2026-02-09 BD completed the spin-off of its Biosciences & Diagnostic Solutions business (combined with Waters Corp via Reverse Morris Trust; BD received ~$4B cash, BD shareholders retained ~39.2% of combined Waters). 'New BD' is now a pure-play MedTech company (Medical Essentials, Interventional, Connected Care, BioPharma Systems). FY2006-FY2025 in the Metrics CSV are the PRE-SPIN CONSOLIDATED entity (includes the divested Biosciences & Diagnostics business) and are NOT used to set the revenue base or historical growth CAGR for the DCF, because they overstate the post-spin company's size and mix. Base-year (FY2026, fiscal year ending 30-Sep-2026) revenue of $19,700M is built two ways that cross-check within ~2%: (a) company-disclosed pro-forma New BD FY2024 revenue of ~$17.8B grown at ~5% (FY25) then ~5.5% (FY26, consistent with the Q3 FY26 print of +5.4% reported YoY and management guiding toward the high end of its range) = ~$19.7B; (b) as-reported quarterly build: Q1 FY26 $4,714M (Oct-Dec 2025, still substantially pre-spin) + Q2 FY26 $4,983M (Jan-Mar 2026, spin closed mid-quarter on Feb 9) + Q3 FY26 ~$5,000M (Apr-Jun 2026, first fully clean post-spin quarter per management commentary) + an estimated Q4 FY26 (Jul-Sep, seasonally the strongest quarter historically) of $5,100-5,400M = $19.8-20.1B total on a mixed (declining-B&D-tail) basis. The two converge near $19.7-20.0B; $19,700M was chosen as the more conservative, cleaner pro-forma anchor. Net debt of $16,100M and shares outstanding of 275.158M are BOTH taken from the Q2 FY2026 (31-Mar-2026) balance sheet -- the latest filed and parsed in the DB -- which already reflects the $2.0B Q2 FY26 ASR and $2.1B of debt retirement funded by Waters proceeds; Q3 FY26 (30-Jun-2026) balance-sheet figures were reported in the Aug-6-2026 release per the Analysis JSON but are not yet in the parsed Metrics CSV/DB, so Q2 is used as the latest fully-parsed anchor (conservative: further buybacks/debt paydown through Q3-Q4 FY26 are not yet reflected, meaning the true current share count is likely somewhat lower and net debt somewhat lower than modeled here). D&A (~11.3% of revenue) and capex (~3.5% of revenue) ratios are anchored to FY2025 consolidated actuals (EBITDA $5,041M minus operating income $2,579M for D&A; capex $760M) on the view that BD's heavy acquisition-intangible amortization (Bard, CareFusion) sits predominantly in the retained MedTech businesses, not in the divested Biosciences & Diagnostics unit, so the ratio should carry over reasonably to New BD; D&A is tapered gradually in the projection as older acquisition intangibles finish amortizing. EBITDA margin FY0 of 24.5% is a house estimate between the Q3 FY26 mixed-basis print (~24.5%) and management's stated intent (BD Excellence productivity program, favorable mix from the new four-segment structure, raised FY26 adjusted operating margin guidance) to expand margin toward the high-20s over the projection horizon (mature at 28% base case). A 10-year horizon is used because the post-spin margin is still ramping (BD Excellence program, stranded-cost removal) and is not yet at a mature flat level in year 5. Buyback_cash of $2,250M (9M FY2026 KPI) reflects real cash outflow (the $2.0B ASR plus ~$250M ordinary buybacks), confirming the flat share count is being actively funded, not merely a modeling convention -- consistent with management's stated capital-allocation priority (at least half of the $4B Waters proceeds to buybacks). Interest income is small (~$26M annualized) and net debt is positive (not net cash), so no interest-income double-count risk exists; the figure is recorded for completeness only and is not material to the valuation.

bear.narrative: Alaris infusion-pump remediation and the CareFusion consent decree remain a persistent cost and management distraction (further FDA actions or penalties beyond the 2024 $175M SEC settlement cannot be ruled out); post-spin separation dis-synergies (stranded IT/corporate costs, management bandwidth split across the four-segment reorganization) run longer and deeper than guided. Hospital capital-spending cyclicality pressures higher-ticket Connected Care equipment sales in a weaker macro. GLP-1/biologics drug-delivery demand growth undershoots the ~$1B-by-2030 target as competitors (glass/syringe capacity build-outs elsewhere) erode BD's share, and tariff/input-cost inflation on resin, glass and other raw materials compresses gross margin faster than BD Excellence productivity gains can offset.

base.narrative: New BD executes the standalone MedTech strategy as guided: BioPharma Systems captures a meaningful share of the GLP-1/biologics drug-delivery buildout (management's own ~$1B incremental-revenue-by-2030 target), Interventional and Connected Care grow at solid mid-single-digit rates, and the BD Excellence productivity program plus removal of the lower-margin Biosciences/Diagnostics mix drives adjusted operating margin from the low-to-mid-20s toward the high-20s over the decade. Alaris/quality remediation and separation-related stranded costs continue but do not derail execution. Leverage glides toward the ~2.5x long-term net-leverage target as free cash flow and residual Waters-proceeds debt paydown continue.

bull.narrative: GLP-1/biologics drug-delivery demand runs ahead of BD's own target (BioPharma Systems becomes a structurally faster-growing, higher-margin segment sooner than guided), Neopak/prefillable-syringe capacity expansions (Columbus NE and future tuck-ins funded by improved post-spin balance sheet flexibility) come online smoothly, and BD Excellence productivity gains compound faster than management's own guidance implies. Alaris/quality remediation costs roll off faster than expected as the consent-decree overhang is resolved, freeing capital and management bandwidth. Multiple tuck-in M&A deals funded by the deleveraged balance sheet add further growth without diluting margin.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 16x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35, moved to 20/50/30. Bear weight raised above the 15% floor because BD carries a live, high-severity regulatory overhang (Alaris/CareFusion FDA consent decree plus the 2024 $175M SEC penalty for misleading investors on the same issue) alongside execution risk from a still-fresh four-segment reorganization and separation from a Reverse Morris Trust transaction completed only seven months before this valuation -- both are concrete, named risks rather than generic pessimism. Bull weight trimmed slightly below 35% because the bull case requires several coincident things to go right (GLP-1 share gains, faster-than-guided margin expansion, additional accretive M&A) rather than one clean catalyst.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
